title: 2014 HMMT February Geometry Problem 1
statement: Let \(O_{1}\) and \(O_{2}\) be concentric circles with radii 4 and 6 , respectively. A chord \(A B\) is drawn in \(O_{1}\) with length 2. Extend \(A B\) to intersect \(O_{2}\) in points \(C\) and \(D\). Find \(C D\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt{2 \sqrt{21}}\) Let \(O\) be the common center of \(O_{1}\) and \(O_{2}\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(A B\). Then \(O M \perp A B\), so by the Pythagorean Theorem, \(O M=\sqrt{4^{2}-1^{2}}=\sqrt{15}\). Thus \(C D=2 C M=\) \(2 \sqrt{6^{2}-15}=2 \sqrt{21}\).
